_comment: Content Wave C2: Olesm Swifttail, Drake [Tactician] / council clerk at the Liscor Guild frontage. Canon (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Olesm_Swifttail): thin, sky-blue-scaled Drake with wildly-patterned blue eyes; earnest, slightly awkward, chess-obsessed, free of the usual Drake prejudices, meticulous with maps and counts; a human once surpassed him at chess and it delighted rather than angered him. The 'resonance' branch is the game's FIRST class-recognition beat -- its entry OPTION and the hub greeting text_variant both gate on classes.tactician (WIDialogue._meets reads _ctx['classes'], id->level; a class gate is visible-but-locked, so a non-Tactician sees the option greyed as a deliberate tease). The 'cisterns' node is a FORESHADOW STUB ONLY -- it does NOT bank heard_about_cisterns. Task C3 extends it into the Q1 'Something in the Cisterns' quest-giver beat (add the effect that banks heard_about_cisterns, which opens the C1 sewer-grate door_when and starts the quest). Opacity rule: no stats shown; class NAME only.

hub.speaker: Olesm
hub.text: Oh — hello. One moment; I'm three columns into a supply tally and if I lose the thread I start again from the granary. ...There. Olesm, council clerk. How can I help?

text_variants.text: Oh — hello. You have the look of someone who counts the exits on the way into a room. A [Tactician]? Truly? I so rarely get to talk shop — sit, sit. Well. Stand. How can I help?

options.text: [Tactician] What's the city's real weak point?
I'll leave you to your tally.

chess.speaker: Olesm
chess.text: Both sides, yes — it's the only honest way to learn how the enemy thinks. You have to want to win as them. A human beat me across this very board once, so thoroughly I nearly thanked her. I did thank her. Best thing to happen to my game in years.

chess_two.speaker: Olesm
chess_two.text: A loss you understand is worth ten wins you don't. That isn't just chess — that's the whole job. If only the Council read reports the way I read a board.

resonance.speaker: Olesm
resonance.text: The weak point? Everyone points at the gap in the south wall. It isn't. It's that Liscor has never been besieged long enough to learn its own supply — morale holds until the third hungry week, and no one has ever counted past the second. ...You already knew that. I can see you did. It is, honestly, a relief not to be the only one in the room doing that arithmetic.

resonance_two.speaker: Olesm
resonance_two.text: I would like that. Genuinely. Bring a board — we'll settle the wall and the war in one afternoon.

cisterns.speaker: Olesm
cisterns.text: Worried is the professional term, yes. The market's had reports — things moving under the grates, a cistern gone foul, a fishmonger who swears something looked back at him from the dark. Probably nothing. I do not care for probably-nothings under a walled city. I'm... still deciding what to do about it.

options.text: Let me know if it turns into a something.
